variants.headline: Looking back: cyclone hits the colony
variants.sub: The colony has been struck by a cyclone.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A cyclone had hit the colony.

A cyclone has hit. That is enough to command attention without a lurid scene supplied by imagination. Think about people. Think about responsibility. But do not let somebody sell a picture of ruined homes or injured neighbours as established news when the report contains no such account.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We criticise {target} on the standard of stewardship surrounding this event. Weather is not a political choice, but responsibility should not disappear behind that fact or become immune from searching public scrutiny.

variants.headline: Looking back: a storm becomes the colony's news
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The colony had been struck by a cyclone.

A cyclone has hit. That is enough to command attention without a lurid scene supplied by imagination. Think about people. Think about responsibility. But do not let somebody sell a picture of ruined homes or injured neighbours as established news when the report contains no such account.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We criticise {target} on the standard of stewardship surrounding this event. Weather is not a political choice, but responsibility should not disappear behind that fact or become immune from searching public scrutiny.

variants.headline: Looking back: the colony faces a cyclone
variants.sub: A cyclone has hit the colony.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: A cyclone had reached {colony}.

A cyclone has hit. That is enough to command attention without a lurid scene supplied by imagination. Think about people. Think about responsibility. But do not let somebody sell a picture of ruined homes or injured neighbours as established news when the report contains no such account.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We criticise {target} on the standard of stewardship surrounding this event. Weather is not a political choice, but responsibility should not disappear behind that fact or become immune from searching public scrutiny.
